surfaceForm: for an R1 institution operating the full pipeline
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch12-observability-EN.tex :: \section{Reference instantiation: Vector + Kafka + OpenSearch + Grafana} (sec:ob-reference), \paragraph{Operational considerations.}
proposedGenericDecision: Express staffing scale by an institution-size/research-intensity role band rather than the Carnegie 'R1' classification, which is a US-specific taxonomy and implicitly anchors the document to one national higher-education system.
rationale: 'R1' is the US Carnegie Classification (very high research activity). Using it as the sizing anchor presumes a US classification regime and is not institution-agnostic. A role-based band (e.g. 'a large research-intensive institution') generalises while preserving the sizing intent.

surfaceForm: on the order of three to five engineers shared with the security operations function
proposedGenericDecision: Keep the FTE envelope as an indicative figure but bind it to the parameterized institution-size tier, since the head-count is implicitly calibrated to the 'R1' (single-jurisdiction) sizing assumption it accompanies.
rationale: The 3-5 engineer figure is only meaningful relative to the institution-size tier it is attached to; once that tier is generalized the figure should be expressed as a tier-relative indicative envelope rather than an absolute the reader may mistake for universal.

surfaceForm: Microsoft Sentinel ... on Log Analytics in a designated regional tenancy
proposedGenericDecision: Replace 'designated regional tenancy' with role-based phrasing tied to the institution's own data-residency requirement (e.g. 'a tenancy in the institution's required data-residency region'), avoiding the implicit assumption of a fixed (EU) region.
rationale: 'designated regional tenancy' silently assumes a single residency region (the document's home EU posture). A generic instantiation must let the residency region follow the adopting institution's jurisdiction.

surfaceForm: the Microsoft estate that is already present at most European universities
proposedGenericDecision: Drop the 'European universities' geographic qualifier and state the prevalence generically (e.g. 'already present at many higher-education institutions'), since the claim is being used as a generic rationale, not a region-bound statistic.
rationale: Restricting the prevalence claim to 'European universities' anchors the reasoning to one region. The value argument holds across higher education generally and should be stated region-agnostically to keep the document institution-agnostic.

surfaceForm: Under the \gls{gdpr} it contributes to Art.~30 ... Art.~33--34 ... and Art.~32
proposedGenericDecision: Treat GDPR as one instantiation of a data-protection regime obligation set (records of processing, breach notification, security of processing) and frame the anchoring against the institution's applicable data-protection regime, naming GDPR as the EU instance.
rationale: GDPR is an EU-jurisdiction-bound regulation presented as the operative regime. An institution-agnostic document should map the observability layer to the generic obligation classes (records, breach notification, security of processing) with GDPR cited as the EU realisation, not the universal one. The specific article numbers (30, 32, 33-34) are GDPR-bound.

surfaceForm: Under NIS2 it operationalises Art.~21(2)(b) (incident handling) and the Art.~23 reporting timelines (24-hour early warning, 72-hour notification, one-month final report)
proposedGenericDecision: Frame the incident-handling and reporting-timeline obligations against the institution's applicable network-and-information-security regime, with NIS2 and its 24h/72h/1-month timelines named as the EU instantiation rather than the universal requirement.
rationale: NIS2 is an EU Directive requiring national transposition; its specific reporting timelines (24h early warning, 72h notification, one-month final report) are jurisdiction-bound. Presenting them as the operative timelines assumes an EU adopter. Generalize to 'the applicable incident-reporting regime' with NIS2 as the EU example.

surfaceForm: the Art.~23 reporting timelines (24-hour early warning, 72-hour notification, one-month final report)
proposedGenericDecision: Keep the concrete timelines only inside an explicitly EU/NIS2-scoped clause; in the generic body refer to 'the early-warning, notification and final-report deadlines defined by the applicable regime'.
rationale: The 24h/72h/one-month values are specific to NIS2 Art.~23; a non-EU adopter has different deadlines. They should be variable-driven so the timeline-reconstruction requirement remains while the numbers localize.

surfaceForm: canonical TAC event schema / correlation_id / TAC session identifier
proposedGenericDecision: No change: 'TAC' is an architecture-internal construct of this policy suite, not an institution-specific term; it generalizes with the architecture.
rationale: TAC (the suite's access/activation abstraction) is part of the portable architecture, not a University-of-Luxembourg-bound term. Flagged only to record that it was assessed and deliberately retained.

surfaceForm: Among what is available in NREN community fora, several research-intensive institutions are reported to operate observability pipelines ...
proposedGenericDecision: Phrasing is already region-agnostic ('NREN community fora', 'research-intensive institutions'); verify no NREN is named and retain as generic precedent framing.
rationale: 'NREN community fora' is a generic category (National Research and Education Networks exist worldwide) and no specific NREN (e.g. RESTENA) is named here. No localization needed, but recorded as assessed since NREN framing can implicitly read European.
